sector_model: payments processing and fintech services: segment revenue and Adjusted EBITDA, customer concentration (Popular), acquisitions and FX, net debt and maturities, capitalized software in capex; nonfinancial FCF model, not bank/insurer/REIT
thesis: EVERTEC runs the ATH debit network, merchant acquiring and bank-processing services in Puerto Rico and, increasingly, Latin America (Brazil via Tecnobank and Dimensa). Q3 2026 revenue 283.0M (+23.8%, about 21% constant currency; acquisitions drive much of it), 9M revenue 805.7M (+17.3%); Latin America segment 9M 384.8M vs 260.2M. GAAP 9M net income to common 59.0M vs 106.0M (-44%) because of higher amortization (+35.7M), SG&A (+53.9M, incl. cyber-incident response), interest (+8.9M), an 8.9M equity-investee impairment and a 30.8% 9M tax rate. Company guides FY2026 revenue 1,088-1,096M and Adjusted EPS 4.00-4.08. TTM (FY2025 - 9M25 + 9M26): net income to common 94.6M, OCF 246.3M, capex incl. capitalized software 98.5M, FCF 147.8M. At the 2026-11-09 close of 33.40 and 59,252,142 shares the market cap is about 1.98B: about 20.9x TTM GAAP net income, 7.5% FCF yield (5.9% after share-based compensation); EV about 2.98B including 1,284.7M debt less 284.1M cash. The 2027 debt wall was removed on 2026-11-05 (term A and revolver refinanced to 2031; 8-K Item 1.01). Cheap-looking on cash flow, but GAAP earnings are depressed and the cyber incident, Popular concentration (22% of Q3 revenue, falling from 29%) and acquisition integration are open questions.
counterthesis: GAAP earnings fell 44% over nine months and the quarter's EPS (0.49) was below last year's (0.51) despite 24% revenue growth, so the low multiple on cash flow may reflect structurally higher amortization, interest and tax. Adjusted EPS (guide 4.00-4.08) excludes acquisition amortization, SBC (31.4M TTM) and deal costs, and management Adjusted EBITDA margin fell to 39.0% from 40.5% as lower-margin Latin America grows. Business Solutions revenue is shrinking (58.6M vs 61.7M) on a 10% Popular discount that began Q4 2025, and Popular is still about 22% of revenue with agreements that include annual minimums only through 2028. Net debt about 1.0B (secured net leverage 2.46x) after 350M of 2025-2026 acquisitions; 3.09M shares were repurchased in 2026 using cash that is also needed for debt. A June 2026 cybersecurity incident at a third-party support platform led to putative class actions in Puerto Rico; no loss estimate is given. Brazil FX and Puerto Rico fiscal and tax-rate risks are real; 2025 revenue growth partly depended on one-off hardware sales and tax-credit sales.
invalidation: Organic revenue growth turning negative, Adjusted EBITDA margin falling below about 37%, a material cyber-incident liability or loss of a major bank client, Popular renegotiating further discounts, leverage rising above about 3x, or GAAP EPS failing to recover as acquisition costs roll off.
